City Council Meeting
MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
City Council, Community Development Financing Authority, Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*
August 20, 2012
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ury at 05:06 p.m. , on August 20, 2012, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.
A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by 5:00 p.m. on August 15, 2012, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. Copies were also posted at the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive, and the Norman P. Murray Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.
*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."
Present:

Council Member Leckness
Council Member Schlicht
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Ury

None

PUBLIC COMMENTS
Joyce Saltzgiver, M.V. (comment read by Mayor Ury): Mrs. Saltzgiver thanked the City for the outstanding job on the new wall on Casta del Sol drive. She noted that the wall is classy and makes the entrance into Casta del Sol look more attractive. Donna Bourassa, M.V.: discussed the decorum at the last City Council Meeting that she attended and expressed disappointment that a Council Member seemed to mock a member of the audience and show disrespect for a fellow Council Member.
Dale Sandore, M.V.: referred to the Kaleidoscope building as a monstrosity and he stated giant signs will be an eyesore. He further stated that the developer made a campaign contribution to Frank Ury and therefore, he is sure that Mayor Ury will vote for new signage.
PUBLIC HEARINGS
20.
Appeal of Planned Development Permit PDP2012-243 and Conditional Use Permit CUP2012-314 filed by Council Member Rhonda Reardon of the Planning and Transportation Commission’s June 11, 2012, Approval of a Petition Submitted by Tom Bergerson, Agent for 7-Eleven, Inc. to Convert an Existing 1,596 sq. ft. Service Bay Building into a "7-Eleven" at the Gas Station at 27271 Trabuco Road, in the CN (Commercial Neighborhood) Zone. No Change is Proposed to the Site’s Existing Gas Station Canopy. Planned Development Permit PDP2012-243 is Filed for Exterior Changes to the Building, Including a New Storefront, and Conditional Use Permit CUP2012-314 is Filed to Permit a Type 20 (Off-Sale Beer & Wine) Alcoholic Beverage License
Director of Community Developement Chuck Wilson presented the staff report.
Associate Planner Christian Murdock presented a slide show depicting the vicinity map, existing and proposed landscaping improvements, and existing and proposed elevations.
Lt. Chris Wilson discussed Police Services’ approach when evaluating the proposed project and he outlined the procedure to assess calls to similar businesses.
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that she appealed the Planning Transportation Commission’s decision regarding the 7-11 project due to her opposition to the proposed 24 hour operation.
All five Council Members announced that they have visited the site of the proposed project.
At the hour of 6:54 p.m., Mayor Ury opened the public hearing.
Applicant Tom Bergerson, Agent for 7-11: presented and overview of the current building and shopping center and discussed the proposed upgrades to the building.
Mike Duke, Orange County 7-11 Market Manager: responded to a question about the owner of the proposed store and he stated that the property is currently owned by 7-11 Corporation until a franchisee is chosen.
Michael Valdez, M.V.: presented a slide show and expressed his opposition to the proposed 7-11 store, most notably he cited concerns with zoning, safety and the sale of alcohol.
The following spoke in opposition to the proposed 7-11 Store at the corner of Marguerite and Trabuco: Byron Barbour, M.V. (submitted a petition with 150 signatures of those opposed to the proposed 7-11); Frank Kirchhoff, M.V.; Johnel Swaim, M.V.; Robbi Doncost, M.V.; Bill Jackson, M.V.; Ken Brackett, M.V.; Megan and Gary Geer, M.V.; Bill Greenfield Jr., M.V.; Michael Leonard, M.V., and Gina Ross, M.V.
The following spoke in support of the proposed 7-11 Store at the corner of Marguerite and Trabuco: Joni Marie O’Neill, M.V. and Gloria Jordan, Gloria Jordan Hair Gallery, M.V.
Bill Ernisse, Vice Chair of the Planning and Transportation Commission, M.V.: recommended that the matter be returned to the Planning Commission if the Council does not reach a consensus.
The following presented written comments in opposition to the proposed 7-11 store: Harry Lenczyk, M.V. and Gary Geer, M.V.
At the hour of 8:10 p.m., Mayor Ury closed the public hearing.
The Council deliberated on the proposed project and discussed concerns with the hours of operation.
Mike Duke, Orange County 7-11 Market Manager, stated that 7-11 would be willing to change the hours to 5:00 a.m. to midnight with the possibility of modifying to a 24-hour operation after one year in business.
Motion made by , seconded by , to
On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:
AYES:
Council Member Kelley, Council Member Leckness, Council Member Schlicht, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, and Mayor Ury

OLD BUSINESS
21.
Ordinance Repealing the Designation of Very High Fire Hazard Severity Zones within the City of Mission Viejo
City Attorney Bill Curley presented the staff report.
Donna Bourassa, Board Member of Mission Viejo Environmental Association (MVEA,) M.V.; expressed concern with the undesirable plant guidelines provided by OCFA and requested a letter from the City documenting that MVEA is exempt from the Vegetative Management Technical Design Guidelines.
Stephen Wontrobski, M.V.: expressed opposition to the SFPA and stated that he believes a homeowner will be required to disclose that their home is in the SFPA to potential buyers and that insurance rates will go up.
The following presented written comments in opposition to the SFPA: Harry Lenczyk, M.V., F. Stephen Masek, M.V.; and Matt Trudell, M.V.
Council Member Schlicht stated for the record that she recognizes the importance of proactive fire prevention and hazard mitigation measures but the public needs to be part of the process. She stated that it has never been disclosed and the public does not understand that there are liabilities that go along with the fire protection zone. She believes there has been a flawed process and there should have been workshops where the public could have been educated along the way. Council Member Schlicht stated that CAL Fire says that it is important that public interests be heard and that the public has been misled.
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon responded that the liabilities that Council Member Schlicht noted are not true and are not accurate. She stated that Council member Schlicht is entitled to her opinion but she is not entitled to her own set of facts. The only reason that the Council considered the SFPA option is because it is transparent for the homeowners and to say anything other than that is wrong, inaccurate, and she can’t let it stand.
Motion made by , seconded by , to

Mr. Rattay responded that there is actually General Fund money that was appropriated for another project and that money is now being allocated for the slope rehab project.
Motion made by Council Member Kelley, seconded by Mayor Pro Tem Reardon, to (1) approve the First Amendment to the existing contract with Spectrum Care Landscape, Inc., to increase the contract in an amount not to exceed $295,000.00; (2) approve the Tenth Amendment to the existing contract with West Coast Arborists, Inc., to increase the contract in an amount not to exceed $55,000.00; and (3) adopt Resolution 12-49 Amending the Fiscal Year 2012-2013 Budget for Costs Related to Marguerite Parkway Slope Rehabilitation.

Council Member Kelley highlighted her attendance at the Prelude in the Park and Symphony in the Cities. She commended City staff for all their hard work and she thanked Target and the Pacific Symphony for providing enriching music for Mission Viejo families.
Council Member Leckness
Council Member Leckness agreed that the Prelude in the Park was a great event and he particularly enjoyed the Waiters’ Race. He also attended a recent dive meet at the Nadadores complex where the announcer described each dive, making it much more interesting to watch and to understand the Olympic divers when he watched the summer games. Council Member Leckness stated that the highlight this month was his attendance at a Mission Viejo Pony League practice game prior to the team's participation in the Pony League World Series. He enjoyed playing ball with the team and he was especially impressed when Council Member Schlicht hit the ball to the outfield.
Council Member Schlicht
Council Member Schlicht reminded residents of two upcoming Mission Viejo Chamber of Commerce events. First, a Business Showcase on September 6 at the Norman P. Murray Community Center followed by the monthly Mixer on September 20 at Atria del Sol. She encouraged residents will attend to find out more about the Chamber. Council Member Schlicht concluded her comments with a quote from Mark Twain: "Truth is the most valuable thing we have."
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon
Mayor Pro Tem Reardon reiterated compliments for the excellent Prelude in the Park and Pacific Symphony event and she stated that she was happy that the black team won the human chess game. She too enjoyed the Mission Viejo Pony League practice game and she stated that she looks forward to honoring the team at an upcoming Council Meeting. Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that she has had recent meetings with constituents on street resurfacing and landscaping matters and, tomorrow night she will attend the screening of a film entitled "Behind the Orange Curtain" about prescription drug overdose deaths in Orange County. She noted that she is hoping to bring the movie to Mission Viejo in October. Lastly, Mayor Pro Tem Reardon announced that she and Mayor Ury attended a meeting with San Clemente Green on issues with San Onofre and she will share additional information at a later meeting.

37.
Update after Completion of the City’s "Improve Don’t Move" Fee Waiver and Reduction Program for Residential and Commercial Building Permits
Mayor Ury stated that the Improve Don’t Move program has concluded, saving over $450,000 for residents. Combined, the residential and commercial programs helped generate approximately $28 million in economic activity in the City of Mission Viejo. He further noted that staff is developing a program to extend the building and planning department hours once a month to assist residents who work during regular business hours. And finally, staff is working with Home Depot on a program that will allow residents to obtain some building permits in the store when they purchase items like water heaters.
Council Member Kelley announced that she attended the Orange County Taxpayers Association’s Roses and Radishes awards ceremony, on behalf of Mayor Ury when he was ill. She was honored to represent the Mayor and the City by accepting the Rose Award for the Improve Don’t Move Program. Council Member Kelley thanked Mayor Ury for bringing this wonderful program to the City.
Mayor Ury thanked his colleagues and staff for their patience while he was out with a detached retina. He thanked Council Member Kelly for attending the Roses and Radishes ceremony and for accepting the award on his behalf.
